(SoCG'26) give constant worst-case guarantees, while for general non-convex objects, bounding-box reductions give just approximation factors that depend on fatness. Against this background, we present a general framework that provides asymptotic polynomial-time approximation schemes (APTAS) for bin packing of any fixed class of simple polygonal regions satisfying just two assumptions. First, covering any object by the grid cells intersecting its interior in any sufficiently fine square grid, relative to the object's bounding box, increases its area by at most a small fraction. Second, the class can be partitioned into a constant number of sequences such that each object in a sequence can be translated to fit inside every preceding object. In particular, certain classes of star-shaped polygons and more general polygonal regions, including some with simple holes, satisfy both assumptions. In addition, our framework does not require a bound on the objects' boundary complexity. We emphasize that our results require no bin augmentation whatsoever and yield explicit, exact rational packings of polynomial encoding length for all input objects.

papers.title: Perception and Utilization of Data Carpentry Tools among Research Scholars at University of Kerala
papers.abstract: Data Carpentry (DC) has been developed to instruct participants on essential concepts, skills, and tools for more effective and reproducible data management. DC emphasizes data literacy, aiming to equip researchers with the skills necessary to retrieve, view, manipulate, analyze, and store their own and other's data in an open and reproducible manner to derive insights from data. The objective of this study was to assess the perceptions and attitudes towards DC among research scholars of University of Kerala and to find out the purpose for which DC tools is used by the research scholars in the University of Kerala. This study requires a sample of 167 and 179 research scholars completed a questionnaire from a total population of 294 using the Krejcie and Morgan formula, with a 95% confidence interval and a 5% margin of error. SPSS version 22 was used to perform descriptive and inferential statistics on the data. 65.9% of research researchers have experience with DC tools. 48.6% of research researchers at the University of Kerala use DC tools primarily for data analysis. 40.2% of research academics identified insufficient access to training as the most significant obstacle they experience while utilizing DC tools in the study. DC emphasizes data literacy, aiming to equip researchers with the skills necessary to access, view, modify, analyze, and manage their own and others' data in an open and repeatable manner to derive insights from data.

papers.title: Observation of pseudospin-locked chiral edge transport in gyromagnetic photonic crystals
papers.abstract: Photonic pseudospins enable selective excitation and routing of light, but perturbations that mix opposite pseudospins can induce backscattering in helical edge channels. Here, we experimentally demonstrate pseudospin-locked chiral edge transport in gyromagnetic photonic crystals, combining pseudospin selectivity with nonreciprocal unidirectional propagation. By jointly engineering lattice deformation and magnetic bias, we control dipolar-quadrupolar band inversions and construct interfaces supporting pseudospin-selective chiral channels. Microwave near-field and transmission measurements reveal a single chiral edge branch that is selectively excited by only one source handedness and exhibits pronounced nonreciprocal transport. Extending this mechanism to multidomain structures, we combine two pseudospin channels into a common waveguide, separate them into distinct outputs, and route them through intersecting interfaces. These configurations realize a nonreciprocal photonic pseudospin multiplexer and demultiplexer, together with a waveguide crossing exhibiting average measured crosstalk of -14.1 and -15.8 dB for its two input channels. Our results present an experimental route to integrating pseudospin-selective channel control with chiral edge transport, providing a foundation for nonreciprocal photonic networks that use pseudospin to organize and route multiple wave channels.

papers.title: Safe Portfolio Learning from Untrusted Predictions: Signed Trust, Abstention, and Cross-Universe Polarity Failure
papers.abstract: Portfolio use of machine predictions must often proceed while the predictions' economic direction, reliability, and timing remain untrusted, and while feedback from overlapping multi-period positions arrives with delay. A controller chooses among Safe, Follow, and Reverse portfolio actions, so signal orientation is learned rather than assumed. A share-adaptive master updates action probabilities from matured Safe-relative rewards, an evidence gate can abstain by transferring unsupported directional probability to Safe, a delayed collateral budget reserves worst-case loss capacity before exposure is funded, and a protected split account caps the capital adaptive decisions may touch. The architecture carries a dual certificate, tracking regret against switching action sequences under delay and one-sided intervention, together with a pathwise collateral safety bound that holds when predictions fail. On a 24-stock development universe a conservative prediction-assisted overlay stays near equal-weight performance at a fraction of the turnover. On a frozen 82-stock holdout, the pre-specified Reverse orientation fails to outperform Equal Weight; a separately labeled post-holdout diagnostic shows that permanently flipping the sign to Follow also does not recover a return edge. Under the post-holdout controller, protected wealth remains within 15.9 basis points of the Safe benchmark throughout. The contribution is safe adaptive use of untrusted predictions, not demonstrated alpha.

papers.title: UniFlow: Unified Multi-Scale Flow Matching for Time Series Generation
papers.abstract: Real-world time series exhibit complex dynamics across multiple temporal resolutions, yet effectively incorporating multi-scale information into generative modeling remains challenging without increasing generative complexity. We propose UniFlow, a unified framework that integrates multi-scale representation learning with efficient non-autoregressive generation through a shared-semantic discrete interface. Specifically, a multi-scale tokenizer employs shared-index voting to consolidate complementary temporal information into a single public-ID sequence, while scale-specific codebooks preserve the information required for reconstruction. Building on this unified representation, we develop geometry-aware categorical flow matching, which initializes transport from learned low-rank anchors and generates public identities non-autoregressively. This design captures multi-scale temporal structure without requiring multiple generative token streams or sequential token decoding. Experiments across four benchmarks and both short- and long-term settings demonstrate improved generative fidelity, strong cross-scale consistency, and substantial inference speedups over representative autoregressive and diffusion-based baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/William-Liwei/uniflow

papers.title: Assignment-Free Swarm Navigation via Adaptive Target-Field Planning and Mean-Shift Exploration
papers.abstract: Mean-shift exploration enables assignment-free swarm shape assembly, but obstacle-constrained navigation additionally requires coordinated adaptation of the desired morphology and its physical execution. This paper presents an environment-adaptive navigation framework that integrates target-field planning, execution regulation, and morphology-preserving mean-shift exploration. A feasibility-aware graph search plans the position, orientation, and morphology of an unlabeled target field without specifying robot-specific goals. An execution-regulated reference manager adjusts field progression and morphology switching using swarm entering, coverage, and lag metrics. A moving-frame controller separates prescribed rigid motion from local mean-shift redistribution and incorporates neighbor interactions and obstacle responses. Simulations and hardware experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework coordinates morphology transitions and collective motion for assignment-free swarm navigation through cluttered environments.

papers.title: The $\mathbb{Z}/2$-equivariant Seiberg--Witten Floer cohomology of the $(2, 1)$-cable is an unknot detector
papers.abstract: We prove that a knot $K \subset S^3$ is the unknot if and only if the $\mathbb{Z}/2$-equivariant Seiberg--Witten Floer cohomology of the double cover branched along the $(2, 1)$-cable of $K$ has no $\mathbb{F}_2[Q]$-torsion. The proof combines the Thom--Gysin exact sequence, the Montesinos trick, and the genus bound for $L$-space surgeries.

papers.title: Radial distortion homography estimation from affine-covariant or orientation-covariant features
papers.abstract: We present minimal solvers for joint homography and radial distortion estimation using affine- or orientation-covariant features. The core contribution is a set of novel constraints that exploit local feature geometry inherent to affine descriptors, enabling solvers that require fewer correspondences than point-based methods. Using modern robust estimation frameworks, we demonstrate that the proposed solvers are advantageous to the current state-of-the-art with a significant speed-up in the presence of outliers while maintaining comparable or superior estimation accuracy. The proposed solvers are tested on both synthetic and real images containing challenging fisheye distortions.

papers.title: Nonreciprocal charge transport in quantum materials: From superconductors to magnetic systems
papers.abstract: Nonreciprocal charge transport, where current flows preferentially in one direction, has become a key topic across quantum materials. This review covers some recent progress in bulk crystals, artificial heterostructures, van der Waals systems, high-temperature superconductors, and magnetic materials. The review discusses both intrinsic origins, such as band-structure effects, and extrinsic ones, including vortex motion, device geometry, and heating artifacts. A central focus is the superconducting diode effect due to its application potential, which shows different critical currents for opposite directions. The review also examines how symmetry breaking, spin-orbit coupling, and magnetic order contribute to the observed responses. However, there remain challenges when many exciting findings lack a unified picture, and the field continues to debate the relative importance of various mechanisms. The review highlights key open questions and suggests future directions, including better experimental standards and device integration. This review aims to give a balanced view of what is known, what is uncertain, and where the field might go next.

papers.title: AI for eGovernance: Leveraging Language Technologies For Digital Inclusion
papers.abstract: The Kenyan government has invested heavily in the digitisation of public service delivery, in line with the Kenya Digital Master Plan 2022-2032. The national eGovernment platform, eCitizen, hosts services that are vital to citizens' livelihoods, including business registration, youth enterprise lending, digital literacy and tax filing. However, the platform faces digital inclusion challenges that limit equitable access for marginalised groups, particularly youth in rural areas and persons with disabilities. This exclusion is driven by a language barrier, since the platform is primarily in English with limited Swahili support, and by a text-only interface that excludes low-literacy and visually impaired users. This paper reports findings from six one-on-one interviews and an eleven-person roundtable discussion across four platforms essential to youth livelihoods: Ajira Digital, Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) iTax, Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) and the Youth Enterprise Development Fund (YEDF). Drawing on these findings, on Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 principles as a design lens for diagnosing eCitizen's accessibility gaps, and on comparator models such as Estonia's Bürokratt and India's Bhashini, the paper proposes a human-centred, systems-minded framework for embedding generative AI and language technologies into eCitizen, including text simplification, neural machine translation, text-to-speech and speech-to-text. The paper argues that, when deployed responsibly with appropriate human oversight, these interventions could meaningfully improve access to government services for linguistically excluded citizens. It also emphasises that AI alone cannot overcome the broader structural barriers, including unemployment and educational inequality, that shape digital exclusion.

papers.title: Reconstructing Fraudulent Strategies in Online Payments via Interpretable Inverse Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Payment fraud causes financial losses and undermines users' trust in web payment services. Although fraud detection is a critical defense for payment security, complex and diverse fraudulent behaviors can still evade detection. Generating fraud samples for data augmentation can broaden detectors' coverage of different fraud patterns. However, existing methods matching the distribution of transaction attributes alone do not ensure that generated sequences preserve the sequential relationships among transaction choices, payment feedback, and subsequent behavioral adjustments. To this end, we propose PaySeqGen, an interpretable inverse reinforcement learning framework that reconstructs fraud behavior policies from fraudsters' observed payment trajectories. We design a mechanism for constructing candidate actions to support plausible payment sequence generation while enabling exploration. The framework also learns interpretable behavioral rewards that capture fraudsters' preferences across different transaction contexts. By alternating between reward learning and policy optimization, the framework reconstructs policies that generate new fraud sequences for detector augmentation and learns interpretable rewards supporting sequential fraud-pattern analysis in real trajectories. Experiments in real-world payment scenarios at Ant International, a leading global digital payment provider, show that PaySeqGen outperforms state-of-the-art generative augmentation methods. Reward-based trajectory analysis also identifies fraud patterns of practical value, helping analyst locating suspicious segments and examine multistep fraud tactics. Evaluation in the deployed system of online payment further confirms its effectiveness.

papers.title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing Detection with Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.abstract: This work investigates the application of Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks to the binary classification of sleep-disordered breathing events in time-series data, aiming to distinguish between apneic and normal breathing episodes. A variational classical--quantum architecture is proposed and evaluated against classical Recurrent Neural Network models. Experiments were conducted on multiple real-world datasets with varying levels of complexity to assess the strengths and limitations of the quantum approach. In the comparative analysis, both classical and quantum models showed comparable performance. The quantum model achieved superior performance on the smallest dataset, while yielding slightly weaker results in the most complex setting. However, the quantum approach exhibited notable strengths, such as competitive performance despite a drastically reduced parameter count and low-qubit regime, as well as good generalization capabilities. These results suggest that, despite current hardware and algorithmic limitations, variational quantum recurrent models represent a promising alternative for time-series classification as Quantum Computing technologies continue to mature.

papers.title: The Pen is Mightier than the Pixel: Natural Textual Unlearnable Example for Large Vision Language Models
papers.abstract: The proliferation of Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs), trained on vast and often sensitive datasets, raised concerns regarding data privacy and unauthorized usage. Unlearnable Examples (UEs), which subtly perturb training data to mislead the models, have emerged as a promising defense method. This paper presents the first exploration of UEs specifically on LVLMs, which poses unique challenges due to their inherent multimodal nature. We propose a novel text-based perturbation method, Natural Textual Unlearnable Examples (NTUE), which can effectively mislead LVLMs by subtly manipulating the image label, establishing a shortcut between an identity of interest and a separate target, without introducing factual misinformation or affecting readability. Comprehensive experiments compared with traditional UE methods demonstrate the superior performance of NTUE. Our findings show that NTUE achieves a high success rate with a poison rate as low as 5%, underscoring its potential as a practical and robust solution for protecting multimodal data in the era of LVLMs.

papers.title: On the Motion of a Point Electric Charge in the Field of Wu-Yang Monopoles in Bertotti-Robinson Spacetimes
papers.abstract: We study the $SU(2)$ Einstein-Yang-Mills system with non-minimal $RF^2$-type couplings of Yang-Mills fields to curvature, formulated with exterior differential forms and a Lagrange-multiplier constraint for the Levi-Civita connection. We show that the conformally flat Bertotti-Robinson geometry $AdS_2\times S^2$ carries the Wu-Yang magnetic pole as an exact solution for arbitrary non-minimal couplings; the couplings only renormalise the radius of the $S^2$. The non-conformally-flat branch of solutions known for this system is recalled. The Hopf fibration $S^3/S^2\cong S^1$ of the gauge group manifold projects the Wu-Yang field on a uniform Dirac-type magnetic field, and the motion of a point electric charge in it is solved in closed form: the charge moves on a cone and oscillates between the horizon and a maximal radius.

papers.title: Intra-unit-cell Josephson scanning tunneling spectroscopy of the cuprate Bi$_{1.2}$Pb$_{0.8}$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+δ}$
papers.abstract: The predominantly $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave pairing symmetry of cuprate superconductors is well established, yet its microscopic manifestation in local Cooper-pair tunneling remains less explored. Here, we investigate Bi$_{1.2}$Pb$_{0.8}$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+δ}$, using Josephson scanning tunneling spectroscopy with a conventional $s$-wave superconducting Pb tip. We observe a zero-bias conductance enhancement whose approximately quadratic dependence on junction conductance is consistent with phase-diffusive Josephson tunneling. Atomic-resolution conductance maps and site-resolved spectra reveal a pronounced intra-unit-cell modulation, with enhanced Josephson response near oxygen sites and strong suppression near copper sites and along diagonal directions. Microscopic calculations incorporating the bilayer electronic structure and realistic Wannier-based tunneling matrix elements reproduce the observed spatial pattern through interference between pairing contributions of opposite signs. Our results reveal how the sign-changing $d$-wave superconducting order parameter manifests itself in atomic-scale Josephson tunneling, providing complementary evidence for unconventional pairing symmetry in cuprates.

papers.title: Think Less, Locally: Local Preference Learning for Reasoning Compression
papers.abstract: Large reasoning models achieve strong performance on challenging tasks, but their long chain-of-thought often incurs substantial inference costs by continuing to deliberate after sufficient information has been obtained. Existing reasoning compression methods primarily operate on reasoning trajectories, paying less attention to the local decision of whether further reasoning is necessary given the current state. We propose LoCo, a local preference learning method for reasoning compression. LoCo detects candidate overthinking states from the model's own traces, freezes the corresponding reasoning prefixes, regenerates shorter verified continuations from the same states, and trains on the resulting state-conditioned preference pairs with DPO. This formulation teaches the model when to continue reasoning and when to conclude, rather than simply encouraging shorter trajectories overall. We construct training data entirely from self-generated mathematical traces and evaluate LoCo on five mathematical and three code generation benchmarks. LoCo reduces completion length by 41.7\%--45.4\% on mathematics and 23.4\%--36.3\% on code, while maintaining or improving accuracy and achieving the best AUC across all code benchmarks. LoCo consistently improves the accuracy-efficiency trade-off on mathematics and transfers effectively to code generation despite math-only training, demonstrating the cross-domain generality of local preference learning for reasoning compression. The code and model will be publicly released at https://github.com/MuyaoYuan/LoCo.

papers.title: Bayesian Cluster-Adjusted Standardised Mean Differences: A Simulation Study
papers.abstract: Reporting standardised mean differences of continuous psychometric measures is omnipresent in psychology. In a randomised controlled trial with a multilevel structure, one can define a cluster-adjusted version of these quantities naturally taking into account heterogeneous residual variances and accounting for the multilevel structure. In this article, we carefully define the underlying location-scale distributional mixed-effects models and derive cluster-adjusted standardised mean differences using partial pooling. Estimating these quantities is best handled using Bayesian statistics, and we perform an extensive Monte Carlo simulation study to test the performance of these metrics under different simulation configurations. We conclude that in order to measure the a-priori heterogeneous treatment effect across clusters in practically relevant scenarios, it is enough to consider random effects only on the location model and not on the scale model. Even under artificial severe heteroscedasticity, this reduced model performs well both in terms of parameter bias and predictive accuracy. The resulting cluster-adjusted standardised mean difference is an average value across clusters, where the heterogeneity is summarised via its standard deviation.

papers.title: NightIQA: A Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for MLLM-Based Nighttime Image Quality Assessment
papers.abstract: Nighttime images are inherently susceptible to complex, compound degradations, making accurate quality assessment exceptionally challenging. Score-based IQA methods condense quality into a single number, lacking the multi-dimensional, language-grounded reasoning required for nighttime evaluation. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a more comprehensive alternative, yet remain constrained by a critical data gap: existing real-world IQA datasets are overwhelmingly daytime-centric and often built from outdated captures, while synthetic alternatives lack nighttime-specific degradation modeling, yielding artifacts far removed from authentic nighttime conditions. To bridge this gap, we present NightIQA, a dataset and benchmark suite purpose-built for MLLM-based nighttime IQA. It comprises three core components: NightIQA-Real, a real-world dataset of 1,769 high-resolution images that we captured ourselves with modern equipment, encompassing six canonical distortion types and structured multi-dimensional annotations; NightIQA-Bench, a benchmark of 1,078 visually grounded multiple-choice questions tailored to MLLM-based nighttime IQA, organized around a four-level evaluation hierarchy spanning Perception, Technical Assessment, Localization, and Reasoning; and NightIQA-Syn, an inherently scalable, scene-aware synthesis pipeline that jointly models global-level and instance-level degradations, with an initial release of 80k high-fidelity images alongside the full generation code. Fine-tuned on NightIQA with Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), Qwen3-VL-8B outperforms open-source IQA methods and achieves higher overall accuracy than leading closed-source models, highlighting the value of domain-specific data and structured supervision.

papers.title: Matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces and tent spaces:characterizations, duality and interpolation
papers.abstract: Let $α\in\mathbb R$, $0<p<\infty$, $0<q,r\le\infty$, and $W$ be a matrix $\mathcal A_p$ weight on ${\mathbb R}^n$. We introduce the matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces $Z^{p,q,r}_α(W)$ and tent spaces $T^{p,q,r}_α(W)$ on the upper half-space and establish their characterizations using reducing operators. We then characterize homogeneous matrix-weighted Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces in terms of the corresponding $Z$-spaces and tent spaces, respectively, using Schwartz kernels satisfying Tauberian and finite moment conditions. Furthermore, we establish duality for the matrix-weighted $Z$-spaces and tent spaces and obtain real and complex interpolation results for these spaces and the associated homogeneous matrix-weighted Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces.

papers.title: RAHC: Rule-Augmented Hyper-Relational Knowledge Graph Completion for Materials Synthesis
papers.abstract: Scientific discovery depends on reusing experimental knowledge, yet records scattered across papers and repositories are often incomplete. In materials synthesis, recovering missing conditions requires reasoning about the target material and the observed context of a specific experiment. Hyper-relational knowledge graphs (HKGs) represent this context through qualifiers, but existing completion methods leave domain knowledge and experimental regularities implicit. We propose RAHC, a rule-augmented HKG framework for single-slot and joint multi-slot synthesis-condition completion. RAHC builds a traceable rule catalog from training records and retrieved literature, retrieves rules for each query-candidate pair, and separately encodes graph structure and rule evidence. Hard rules constrain candidate validity, while soft rules guide ranking. RAHC-G aggregates rules using global reliability; RAHC-Q additionally learns query-specific relevance. Gated fusion combines structural and rule representations, while tuple-conclusion rules provide cross-condition evidence for joint completion. Experiments on five materials-synthesis datasets show improvements in single-slot and joint completion under Semi-inductive and Open-Answer Inductive settings, with Semi-inductive MRR gains of up to 15.6% over MAYPL. RAHC also improves performance on the entity-disjoint ILPC'22 Small benchmark, supporting transfer to fully inductive KG completion. These results support experimental condition selection, synthesis planning, and the reuse of scientific knowledge.

papers.title: Four problems about the irreducible determined $T_0$-topologies
papers.abstract: We answer four questions on irreducible determined $T_0$-topologies and a related question on monotone determined topologies posed by Xu, Yang and Luo (Topology Appl.\ 382 (2026), 109762). For every $T_0$ topology $τ$, the family $τ_r$ used to define its irreducible-derived topology is already a topology and preserves all nonempty irreducible subsets and their closures. Consequently, the least irreducible determined refinement is obtained in one step: $τ_r=\rd(τ)=\Rd(τ)$. For an arbitrary poset $P$, we describe the weakest order-compatible irreducible determined topology $ρ(P)$ using Dedekind--MacNeille cuts and a finite-cover condition involving principal lower sets. The Scott space of the binary-prefix domain provides a common counterexample to saturated heredity for irreducible determined spaces and monotone determined spaces: its maximal-point subspace is Cantor space. We also describe $ρ(P)$-closure by iterating an irreducible-cut operator, characterize Scott continuity of this operator, and give an example requiring two applications of the cut operator. A finite-decomposition condition extends the topology and closure-preservation results to general subset systems. For the Rudin and well-filtered determined systems, we exhibit a common $T_1$ example whose first and second derived topologies are the co-countable and discrete topologies, respectively. Thus the first derived topology need not be determined by the same subset system.

papers.title: Asymptotic Optimality of $cμ$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference, the process by which a pre-trained model receives an input prompt and generates output tokens sequentially, has become increasingly important with the widespread deployment of LLM-based applications. As inference workloads continue to scale, GPU memory has emerged as a critical bottleneck: the long input prompts and generation sequences common in agentic and reasoning workloads lead to substantial key-value (KV) cache usage. In this paper, we study the resulting online scheduling problem from a queueing perspective. Requests arrive stochastically with heterogeneous prompt and output lengths, undergo prefill and autoregressive decode, and compete for a finite KV-cache capacity. Unlike classical queueing models, the duration of a processing step depends on both prefill computation and KV-cache I/O, so service capacity is jointly determined by computation, memory access, and memory occupancy. We develop a fluid model that reduces the system to a multiclass single-server queue with effective service rates capturing computation, memory access, and memory capacity. This fluid analysis yields a $cμ$ priority rule, where the effective service rate $μ$ is jointly determined by computational speed, memory bandwidth, and memory capacity. We prove that this rule minimizes cumulative holding cost in the fluid model and, for a finite workload, also minimizes completion time and maximizes full-run output-token throughput. We then construct a feasible scheduling policy for the original finite system and prove that its scaled dynamics converge to the optimal fluid policy. Finally, experiments on a real LLM serving engine using an NVIDIA H800 show that practical implementations of the proposed priority rule substantially reduce average latency while maintaining high throughput relative to existing scheduling policies.

papers.title: On the Complexity of Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization with Exact Proximal Oracles
papers.abstract: Finite-sum nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax problems arise in adversarial training and distributionally robust learning. Their known lower bounds cover only linear-span algorithms, zero-respecting algorithms, or a restricted proximal protocol. They leave open the power of exact component proximal steps, whose responses are global saddle points of regularized component problems and can expose directions that gradients do not reveal. We show that neither unrestricted adaptivity nor exact proximal access improves the polynomial complexity. We consider $n$ components with joint mean-squared smoothness $L$ and condition number $κ$, started from a point with primal gap at most $Δ$ and joint gradient norm at most $\sqrt{2LΔ}$. For $\varepsilon^2/(LΔ)$ below a universal constant, every randomized adaptive algorithm with exact component values, gradients, and proximal responses needs $Ω(n+\min\{\sqrt n\,κ,n^{3/4}\sqrtκ\}LΔ/\varepsilon^2)$ component queries in the worst case to find an $\varepsilon$-stationary point of the value function. A method using only component gradients attains this rate up to a factor $\log^2(2+κ)$, including initialization. Zhou (arXiv:2610.04944) concurrently proves the same rate for zero-respecting first-order methods. In our hard instances, every component admits proximal steps with the same step sizes, and a response for a component reveals hidden directions only up to the first one assigned to another component.

papers.title: Where Is the Truth When AI Agents Disagree? Dependence-Aware Belief Propagation for Unsupervised Truth Discovery (Extended Version)
papers.abstract: LLM agents often give conflicting answers to the same question, and many deployed agents are variants of one base model, so their errors are correlated. We study truth discovery among such agents: inferring the true answer and each agent's reliability without labels. Classical truth-discovery and crowdsourcing estimators reward an agreeing bloc and can fall below majority vote. We propose BP-TD, which adds per-agent decorrelation weights to mean-field variational inference on a one-coin Dawid-Skene model, so that agents sharing a base model count together as about one vote. Its first iteration is exactly a weighted vote; later iterations estimate agent reliability. With 13 local agents on MMLU, BP-TD beats majority vote without any labels (0.716 vs. 0.624 on 160 questions; 0.707 vs. 0.674 on 10,000) and ranks agents by their true accuracy, which classical estimators invert. The gain depends on the pool: over 2,852 sub-pools of four benchmarks, decorrelation helps when the largest correlated bloc is weaker than the other agents and hurts when it is the strongest, and we found no label-free statistic that tells the two cases apart. Labels change the picture quickly: with 20 labelled questions, selecting the single best agent is more accurate than every aggregator we tested on MMLU, ARC and TruthfulQA.

papers.title: Extracting System Prompt of LLM Services in Complex (Agentic) Settings: Hierarchical Optimization and Reliable Evaluation Metrics
papers.abstract: System prompt is a critical intellectual property of large language model (LLM) services. To analyze its leakage, prompt extraction attacks have been extensively studied. However, we validate that existing attacks substantially degrade on recent LLM services, whose complexity has evolved in both the prompt itself and system-level constraints. Specifically, (1) system prompts become longer and more structured to contain pre-defined tool schemas, execution logic, safety guardrails, etc., and (2) only the final post-processed outputs (e.g., agent's actions) but not the raw textual response can be observed. In this paper, we address the above increased complexity by proposing Extraction with Hierarchical Optimization (ExtraHerO), which (1) decomposes the prompt extraction into a hierarchical reconstruction process with a pre-defined structural prompt template, and (2) iteratively updates the adversarial query with guidance of feedback-template differences to observe diverse outputs. In particular, we monitor the information gain of attack optimization to early stop or reset it for a good trade-off between effectiveness and efficiency. We also find that existing evaluation metrics for prompt fidelity can be misleading because they do not account for structural information. Therefore, we rely on global textual similarity and prioritize structural keywords. Moreover, we introduce a system-level metric, adversarial utility, to measure the help of prompt extraction for real-world downstream attacks. Experimental results demonstrate the consistent superiority of ExtraHerO, with average improvements of 12.5\% (fidelity), 2.3\% (functionality), and 6.0\% (adversarial utility) on chatbots, and 12.2\%, 34.3\%, and 30.5\% on agents.

papers.title: Study of enhancing the signal-background separation for the Higgs boson production in association with a single top-quark in $pp$ collisions at the LHC
papers.abstract: In this paper, a multivariate analysis based approach for enhancing the extraction of the rare Standard Model (SM) process being studied - Higgs boson production in association with a single top quark (tH) - from the prevailing background processes is presented. The analysis was performed using a Monte Carlo generated dataset simulating the outcomes of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). A deep fully connected neural network was developed for signal-background discrimination, incorporating a masking mechanism designed to suppress the contribution of input variables associated with objects that were not reconstructed in a given event. The performance of the masked architecture was evaluated on independent Monte Carlo samples. The results of the proposed methodology are compared with a conventional cut-based approach in terms of the statistical significance of the tH production channel. The developed framework was tested using a simulated dataset corresponding approximately to the combined statistical samples of LHC Runs 1, 2, and 3.

papers.title: Pushforwards of lc pairs under morphisms to abelian varieties
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a morphism from a log canonical pair $(X,Δ)$ to an abelian variety $A$ and $D\sim_{\mathbb Q}m(K_X+Δ)$ a Cartier divisor on $X$ with $m>1$ a rational number. We prove that $f_*\mathcal{O}_X(D)$ is globally generated after pullback by an isogeny. Our methods involve birational geometry, mixed Hodge modules and singular Hermitian metrics with the minimal extension property. Moreover, we provide simple counterexamples where the above result fails for plt pairs when $m=1$ and where the existence of Chen--Jiang decompositions fails for plt pairs for any $m\ge1$.

papers.title: Disruption limits around triaxial bodies and implications for ring-bearing minor bodies
papers.abstract: The classical Roche limit is often used as a boundary between ring-dominated and satellite-dominated regions, although it is derived for a self-gravitating fluid satellite orbiting a spherical primary. This assumption is poorly suited to ring-bearing minor bodies, which are often triaxial. Here, we compute the equilibrium figures and disruption limits of inviscid fluid satellites orbiting triaxial primaries, modelling their gravity fields through J2 and C22. The primary's oblateness and equatorial asymmetry shifts the disruption limit outward relative to the classical Roche limit, with C22 dominating the correction at sufficiently high values, which require highly oblate primaries. The disruption location also depends on the primary's orientation, defining a radial disruption region rather than a single limit in non-double-synchronous systems. Increasing orbital inclination shifts the limit inward, significantly so only at high inclinations. Symbolic regression provides an empirical expression for the disruption limit around triaxial primaries, which we apply to ring-bearing minor bodies. The correction is most relevant for Haumea and Chariklo, whereas the rings of Chiron and Quaoar located beyond the classical Roche limit remain outside the disruption region for realistic particle densities. This indicates that treating the disruption limit as a strict boundary between ring-dominated and satellite-dominated regions is an oversimplification, since the long-term survival of a ring also depends on collisional evolution, particle properties, and resonant confinement driven by the primary's non-axisymmetric gravity field.

papers.title: Generic factorizations and alternating direction method for fixed-rank approximation of matrix polynomials
papers.abstract: We present an algorithm for approximating a given matrix polynomial of degree $d$ by a matrix polynomial of prescribed rank and degree at most $d$. The method builds on recent advances in the theory of generic eigenstructures and factorizations of matrix polynomials with bounded rank and degree. We also give a specialized treatment of the case of matrix pencils (degree one matrix polynomials), motivated by its particular theoretical and practical importance. Lastly, numerical experiments are reported to assess the performance of the proposed approach and to compare it with existing methods.

papers.title: Current-Future Rate Tradeoffs in ISAC Under Random Path Changes
papers.abstract: In mobile wireless links, motion changes path directions and visibility, and blockage can shift communication to a different propagation path. Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) allows a base station (BS) to use echoes of data transmissions to monitor these changes and guide subsequent beam selection. Illuminating objects that govern future path availability may reduce the beamforming gain on the current communication route. Existing sensing-communication tradeoffs and dynamic beam-control frameworks do not directly quantify the future communication gain from this current-rate sacrifice. We quantify sensing value by the future-rate gain enabled by echo-adaptive beam selection. We derive explicit expressions for the future communication gain and the net gain after accounting for the current-rate loss. The analysis uses a coupled communication-echo channel with binary-state Markov motion over a finite burst informed by one processed echo. We show that monitoring is worthwhile when its future-rate gain exceeds the current loss, while more informative observations yield zero additional future rate if they cannot change any future optimal beam. We derive interpretable gain bounds exposing the roles of improved scene discrimination, motion memory and future beam-rate differences. Reciprocal-channel tests demonstrate positive net accumulated-rate gains from monitoring a moving blocker during reflected-path service, including continuous position uncertainty.

papers.title: Training Specialist LLMs on Your Phone: Forward-Only Optimization via Block-Spectral Coordinates
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) on personal devices keep user data local, but limited memory restricts their general capability. Since most user-specific tasks do not require the breadth of frontier models, a practical solution is to adapt a shared on-device model into lightweight specialists. However, backpropagation is prohibitive in memory, and users rarely provide labeled data. We present MobileSpec, a system that trains specialists with forward passes alone and learns from automatically checked task outcomes, as in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Because forward-only updates are built from random perturbations, training is efficient only when these perturbations resemble the weight changes of RLVR, which largely preserve the singular values of pretrained weights and rotate their singular vectors. The core algorithm of MobileSpec, FuRA-S, produces such perturbations while training only the block-spectral coordinates of pretrained weights, namely the singular values of their column blocks. As we show theoretically and empirically, rescaling these blocks independently shifts their relative contributions to each weight matrix and thereby rotates its singular vectors. Since this update can be rewritten as a transformation of the layer input, FuRA-S also adapts INT4 models without modifying their weights. With specialists of only 1-5 MB that update 0.015-0.05% of the parameters, MobileSpec raises the success rate of a phone-use agent from 6-23% up to 89-100% and trains a personalized 8B model on an iPhone 16 Pro overnight. On RLVR benchmarks, FuRA-S is competitive with full-parameter evolution strategies (ES) and outperforms ES over LoRA adapters and quantized ES on INT4 models.

papers.title: Construction of New Complete Complementary Codes Using Extended Boolean Functions and Permutations
papers.abstract: Complete complementary code (CCC) is a crucial component in the design and optimization of modern wireless communication systems, particularly in addressing challenges related to interference, spectral efficiency, and signal quality. The design of CCCs is an active area of research, as it directly impacts the number of users that can be supported interference-free in the system. In the literature, CCC constructions are restricted by a set size smaller than the sequence length. In this paper, we introduce a novel construction method for CCCs based on the extended Boolean functions (EBF) that overcome existing restrictions by including a set size bigger than the sequence length. Further, the proposed construction uses functions which are new in literature and provide us with new CCCs. This is also the very first construction where row PMEPR is also bounded by $n$ for a set size in the form of power of $n$.

papers.title: Reconstructing Rayleigh--Bénard flows from temperature-only measurements using the Ensemble Kalman Filter
papers.abstract: Reconstructing the full state of a multiscale chaotic system from observations of only a subset of its degrees of freedom is a central problem in data assimilation. Turbulent Rayleigh--Bénard convection offers a paradigmatic example, for which Charney conjectured that temperature measurements alone should suffice to determine the velocity field. Synchronization-based methods such as nudging and direct replacement nonetheless fail in chaotic regimes, because they require the measurement of the determining modes of the system, a set to which the velocity belongs but the temperature does not. Here we show that the Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF), equipped with a proper inflation scheme, removes this asymmetry by exploiting the flow-dependent cross-covariances between temperature and vorticity, and recovers the velocity from noisy and spatio-temporally sparse temperature data alone. We assess the filter in two chaotic regimes of two-dimensional bulk convection by means of a scale-by-scale spectral analysis. When the whole temperature field is observed, both fields synchronize with the true state at all resolved scales, with the temperature estimate becoming even more accurate than the measurements themselves for sufficiently frequent observations. Equispaced observation networks preserve this full-spectrum synchronization down to a threshold density, below which only the largest scales remain synchronized, as also happens when observations are confined to a subdomain. We conclude that Charney's conjecture is numerically verified in two-dimensional turbulent convection when the assimilation is performed using a properly calibrated EnKF.

papers.title: Accelerating Offloading-Based MoE Inference by Interleaving Concurrent Requests
papers.abstract: Expert offloading enables large mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models to run locally, but conventional batching stalls the GPU while missing experts are fetched. A popular remedy, known as prefetching, is to predict what experts will be needed soon and fetch them using idle link bandwidth. Imprecise prediction, however, wastes bandwidth and GPU memory on fetching unnecessary experts. Our key finding is that prefetching can be harmful when there is an expert cache in GPU memory. This is because as the cache includes more necessary experts, expert prediction becomes less precise. Our key insight is that proper request scheduling beats prefetching. Building on this insight, we present Bevy, an MoE inference system based on runahead inference for concurrent requests. A request whose experts are available can run ahead to later layers while other requests wait for fetches, revealing the experts it needs next. Bevy can then fetch the missing experts so identified while computing ready requests, overlapping computation and fetching without predicting expert selections. Running requests separately, however, repeats reads of shared weights in GPU memory and increases compute time. To limit this cost, Bevy's self-balancing scheduler batches ready requests at each layer and prioritizes lagging requests, adapting their grouping as expert availability changes. Across two local platforms, Bevy delivers up to 3.46$\times$ the decode throughput of llama.cpp and up to 1.55$\times$ that of the fastest prefetching baseline.

papers.title: Regularity of geodesics in the spaces of convex and plurisubharmonic functions III
papers.abstract: In this note, we study the regularity of solutions to the geodesic equation in the space of plurisubharmonic functions in a general Reinhardt domain. Our findings resolve a problem left open from our previous note [AD26].

papers.title: Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning objectives that maximize expected return can concentrate probability mass on a small subset of high-reward outcomes, limiting diversity when multiple distinct solutions are desirable. We introduce Density-Aware Reward Scaling (DARS), a simple reward-processing mechanism that promotes reward-proportional sampling in continuous outcome spaces while retaining standard policy-gradient training. DARS estimates the local density of outcomes within each on-policy rollout group and inversely scales rewards by this density. The method requires no learned density model, auxiliary objective, critic, or modification to the underlying policy-gradient objective. In a controlled multimodal navigation task, DARS-GRPO avoids the single-mode collapse exhibited by GRPO and closely recovers the target mode allocation. Applied to text-to-image prompt adaptation, DARS-GRPO consistently improves image and prompt diversity across datasets, Policy LMs, and reward settings while maintaining good semantic alignment. These results show that density-aware reward scaling provides a lightweight way to improve coverage of diverse high-reward outcomes within existing reinforcement-learning pipelines.

papers.title: Hidden Symmetries of the Kepler Problem and Jacobi's Theorem
papers.abstract: We present a geometric derivation of the hidden symmetries of the Kepler problem, combining a duality for central-force systems, obtained by interchanging positions and velocities, with a generalized form of Jacobi's theorem. Applied to the dual Kepler problem, this theorem identifies Kepler hodographs of prescribed energy with geodesics of a metric of constant curvature. After adjoining one point at infinity, the resulting geometry is complete. Its Killing vector fields induce a finite-dimensional Lie algebra of infinitesimal symmetries on the corresponding energy hypersurface. The distinguished point at infinity determines a canonical decomposition of the Killing algebra into two vector subspaces, whose associated Noether invariants recover angular momentum and the Runge-Lenz vector.

papers.title: Space--time Runge approximation for weakly viscous nonlocal waves and identification of coefficients
papers.abstract: We study very weak solutions and Runge approximation for weakly viscous nonlocal wave equations with elastic term $(-Δ)^su$ and dissipative term $(-Δ)^r\partial_tu$, where $0\leq r<s$. For time-dependent potentials satisfying a smallness condition, we establish a transposition theory for sources in the dual of the natural space--time energy space. Under explicit nonlocality and nonresonance assumptions, we prove Runge approximation in $L^2(0,T;\widetilde H^s(Ω))$ and in $L^2(0,T;\widetilde H^s(Ω)) \cap H^1_0(0,T;\widetilde H^r(Ω))$. As an application, partial exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann measurements uniquely determine a bounded, nonnegative, time-dependent coefficient in the nonlinear velocity damping term $q|\partial_tu|^{p-2}\partial_tu$ for $0<r<s$ and $2<p\leq 2+4r/n$. The proof establishes the small-amplitude response by energy estimates, weighted $L^p$ monotonicity convergence, and a linear Green identity, then applies adjoint Runge approximation followed by a forward velocity approximation in $L^2$. No smallness or positive lower bound is imposed on the nonlinear damping coefficient.

papers.title: Weakly viscous nonlocal wave equations: forward theory, Lebesgue Runge approximation, and inverse problems
papers.abstract: We study forward and inverse problems for weakly viscous nonlocal wave equations with elastic term $(-Δ)^s u$ and dissipative term $(-Δ)^r\partial_tu$, where $0\leq r<s$. For time-dependent potentials in suitable $L^\infty(0,T;L^p(Ω))$ classes, we establish finite energy well-posedness, strong continuity in time, and an energy identity by parabolic regularization and time-regularization arguments. Under explicit nonlocality and nonresonance assumptions on the fractional orders, we prove Runge approximation in $L^2(0,T;\widetilde H^r(Ω))$ and hence in $L^2(Ω\times(0,T))$. As an application, partial exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann measurements uniquely determine the potential in all three exponent regimes of the Runge theorem, including integer elastic orders with noninteger dissipative orders. The recovery argument combines equality of solutions with the same exterior input, unique continuation or the entanglement principle, and a single Lebesgue-space Runge approximation. It applies to the full admissible potential class, without spatial boundedness, sign, or smallness assumptions.

papers.title: Global Trace Condition for Injective Transition Graphs
papers.abstract: We formulate the global trace condition, GTC, for cyclic proofs as a particular case of the size-change termination condition, or SCT. We express cyclic proofs through a variant of size-change graphs, called transition graphs, whose edges are labelled by (finite) bipartite relations. We show that injective transition graphs suffice to encode cyclic pre-proofs for a variant of Brotherston and Simpson's sequent calculus with inductive definitions. The injectivity of transition graphs corresponds to restricting SCT to fan-in-free graphs. Then we prove that an essentially weaker condition implies SCT in this case, and hence GTC.

papers.title: ReSI-Math: Exploring Recoverable Capability Frontiers for Efficient Reasoning Improvement
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an effective approach for improving mathematical reasoning in large language models. However, a fundamental question remains: when a model fails to solve a problem, does it truly lack the underlying capability? In this work, we reveal that direct failure does not necessarily imply inability. Some reasoning failures can be recovered by exploring the model's own trajectories, exposing a recoverable capability frontier: a policy-dependent region where solutions are not reliably generated through direct decoding but can be elicited through trajectory-level search. Based on this observation, we introduce ReSI-Math, a framework that explores recoverable capability frontiers and converts recovered capabilities into data-efficient RLVR supervision. ReSI-Math uses Self-Judge-guided evolutionary search to identify recoverable failures under a fixed policy and adaptively selects frontier problems for sequential RLVR as the policy evolves. On Qwen3-VL-8B, correct-incorrect trajectory crossover produces 272 verifier-confirmed correct offspring from 621 attempts (43.8%). After three sequential one-shot RLVR stages, the MATH500 and WE-MATH average improves from 78.71 to 80.16. Under matched single-problem RLVR, random selection reaches only 53.31 versus 54.16 for frontier-guided Q1.

papers.title: Near-linear-Time Sampling of the Ferromagnetic Ising Model at the Tree Uniqueness Threshold
papers.abstract: We give a near-linear-time sampler for the zero-field ferromagnetic Ising model throughout the tree-uniqueness regime, including the threshold itself. The method also gives sampling algorithms for the XY and integer Potts models. On an $n$-vertex graph with $m$ edges and maximum degree at most $Δ$, we obtain the following expected-work bounds, with total variation error at most $\varepsilon$. 1.Near-linear Ising sampling. For $Δ\ge3$, the work is $O(n+m\log^3(n/\varepsilon))$ throughout the tree-uniqueness regime, including the threshold $β=Δ/(Δ-2)$. 2.Almost-linear XY sampling. For $Δ\ge8$, we sample the XY model in $\widetilde O(m+n^{1+o(1)})$ expected work at inverse-polynomial accuracy up to and including the robust phase-transition threshold on the $Δ$-regular tree. 3.Near-linear Potts sampling. For integer $q\ge3$, we sample the $q$-state Potts model in $\widetilde O(n+q^{O(1)}m)$ expected work whenever $β-1\le 0.1(β_{\mathrm{od}}(q,Δ)-1)$, where $β_{\mathrm{od}}$ is the ordered/disordered coexistence parameter. We express the even-subgraph representation of critical Ising as a polymer model that admits near-linear-time sampling, thereby bypassing the critical slowdown of Glauber and Swendsen--Wang dynamics. Building on the low-degree approximation approach of Miao and Yin, we establish general spectral conditions for fast polymer sampling. We verify these conditions through explorations that also implement the sampler efficiently, and apply the same framework to flow representations of the XY and Potts models. We also establish polynomial-time counting and sampling for the ferromagnetic XY model at every fixed temperature.

papers.title: Kierston & KierstonBench: Simulation of Allentown, PA and Evaluation of Language Models in Crime Investigation and Surveillance Tasks
papers.abstract: Large language models are candidates for collecting and analyzing records in criminal investigations and mass surveillance. Their capability and accuracy in this work cannot currently be measured. Real deployments lack the ground truth needed to score a model's conclusions, and no benchmark evaluates these capabilities in a simulated environment. We present Kierston, a city-scale simulation engine, and KierstonBench, a benchmark that tests these capabilities against known simulated events. Kierston models approximately 125,000 residents of Allentown, Pennsylvania, generating their daily activities and the telecommunications, financial, administrative and license-plate records that surveillance and investigative systems collect about them. These records derive from a common behavioral timeline and are distributed across sources representing separate providers. Models investigate through a restricted records interface, linking observations across sources without access to the underlying simulation. The benchmark comprises 32 task families covering record linkage, routine reconstruction, incident investigation and assessment of deceptive accounts. In an evaluation of sixteen language models, most could not perform records investigation and submitted identifications the records did not support. A small number of frontier models solved most of the tasks and abstained when evidence was insufficient. In some cases these models still fell for common deceptions and assumptions, and none replaced an investigator.

papers.title: Optimal Approximation for Constrained Correlation Clustering via Repulsion
papers.abstract: The best-known approximation factor for constrained correlation clustering stood at three for nearly two decades, until a recent improvement to below $16/7$. We give a randomized polynomial-time $(2+\varepsilon)$-approximation using \emph{Repulsion}, a recursive operation that separates a metric ball from its complement. Repulsion naturally respects hard constraints and admits a short potential-based analysis; as a warm-up, radius-$2/3$ Repulsion rounds the standard metric LP into a feasible partition of cost at most three times its objective. The $(2+\varepsilon)$-approximation takes a two-stage approach, first removing must-links with arbitrarily small loss in the approximation ratio. The second stage combines lossless, constraint-aware preclustering with the bounded sub-cluster LP framework of Cao, Cohen-Addad, Lee, Li, Newman, and Vogl (STOC 2024). Repeated positive conditioning and sampling produce candidate sets, which radius-one Repulsion partitions into feasible clusters at controlled cost. We also give an approximation-preserving reduction from vertex cover to cluster deletion, a special case with only cannot-links. Apart from establishing a matching factor-two hardness threshold under the Unique Games Conjecture, it motivates our two-stage approach and Repulsion.

papers.title: Who Is Doing the Thinking? Characterising Human Agency in First-Year Students' AI Interactions
papers.abstract: When students use generative AI to produce their work, the learning process becomes invisible. Established frameworks such as Bloom's taxonomy then classify the cognitive level of what the AI produced, not what the student contributed. We propose the Human Agency Depth Taxonomy (HADT), a preliminary six-tier taxonomy that classifies the engineering contribution a student makes in a prompt, independent of the AI's output. HADT combines three dimensions: contextual bandwidth, engineering abstraction and student agency. We applied HADT to 962 prompts from 105 students' structured AI Journals in an AI-permissive, first-year software engineering course of 145 students, and examined how agency changed over ten journalled weeks. Most prompts (84.2%) carried some student contribution beyond delegation. Agency tracked the development lifecycle. Architecture-discovery prompts dominated the requirements phase (48% of turns) and fell to 5-12% from week 9, while prompts analysing existing systems rose during build and verification (odds ratio 2.88, with turns clustered by student). Two-thirds of the variance in tier lay within students, so agency depended more on the phase of work than on the student. A turn-level rise in delegation in deadline weeks did not hold once turns were clustered by student. Explicitly specifying constraints on the AI's output was rare throughout, which we interpret as a knowledge bottleneck for novices rather than a gap in instruction. We discuss implications for course and assessment design, and for using HADT as a formative lens on how students engage with AI.

papers.title: Reducing Logprob Without Causal Verification: Diagnosing SAE-Based PII Suppression in LLMs
papers.abstract: SAE-based feature-level interventions to suppress PII leakage in LLMs are primarily evaluated by log-probability reduction. We show that this criterion cannot distinguish feature specific suppression from a magnitude artifact: a direction-agnostic effect of sufficiently large activation perturbations. Across 36 (model, layer, PII type) cases, we compare selected SAE feature interventions with coherencematched random direction controls using logprob and rank-aware metrics. While 17 cases (47%) appear successful under logprob-only evaluation, only 1 case (2.8%) passes our multimetric framework. The rest reveal two failure modes: random directions outperform selected features, and feature selection collapse across PII types. These results indicate that existing evaluations cannot verify whether interventions target causal pathways of PII leakage. A 9,000 run causal mediation feasibility study corroborates this: the verifier separates candidates reliably, but correlation-selected candidates rarely pass it. We therefore propose a new research mission for NLP: causally grounded PII suppression through circuit-level localization and causal mediation analysis.

papers.title: On the Onsager--Machlup functional of the infinite-dimensional angular central Gaussian distribution and related measures
papers.abstract: The Onsager--Machlup functional of a probability measure is a generalisation of the negative logarithm of the probability density function, defined precisely using the ratios of masses of balls in the limit of vanishing radius. It plays an important role in several areas of applied mathematics because its minimisers can be understood as modes of the measure. We show that the Onsager--Machlup functional of the angular central Gaussian measure on the unit sphere of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space---i.e., the radial projection of a centred Gaussian measure with covariance operator $C$---is constant on the finite-dimensional sphere spanned by the eigenvectors of leading eigenvalue under $C$, and takes the value $+\infty$ elsewhere. We discuss the consequences of this extreme concentration of mass for maximum a posteriori estimation in Bayesian inverse problems with an angular central Gaussian prior.

papers.title: LIPS-PC: Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification
papers.abstract: In single-pixel (ghost) imaging, known illumination patterns probe an object and a detector with no spatial resolution returns one number per pattern. Each measurement costs acquisition time and photons and, for ionizing probes, contributes to delivered dose. Motivated by automated radiographic defect screening, where a class label suffices, we introduce Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification (LIPS-PC). The patterns are learned end-to-end while the measurement operator remains one fixed linear matrix, identical for every input. We parameterize it as a residual correction to a two-dimensional discrete cosine transform (2D-DCT), $D=D_{\mathrm{base}}+Δ$, and jointly train the correction and a compact classifier using cross-entropy, without a reconstruction objective. This yields a task-driven linear embedding through optimization. We evaluate LIPS-PC numerically on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST under a controlled protocol, then on RIAWELC, a real industrial X-ray weld-radiograph dataset. Across five budgets, $M\in{8,16,32,64,128}$, corresponding to sampling ratios from below 1% to 12.5%, the learned operator outperforms the best tested fixed transform by 9-15 percentage points at $M=8$ on all three datasets. Its eight-measurement accuracy requires roughly 16-32 measurements with the best fixed transform, indicating a $2\times$ to $4\times$ saving at comparable accuracy. The advantage generally shrinks as $M$ increases, with a small reversal on RIAWELC at higher budgets. These results show that learning what to measure is especially valuable when measurements are scarce.

papers.title: Replica-Aware Split Inference for Edge IoT Systems
papers.abstract: Split Inference (SI) addresses the hardware resource limitations of Internet of Things (IoT) devices by distributing tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) model segments across multiple IoT devices. However, a device failure can interrupt the inference pipeline. This paper proposes a replica-aware recovery approach that deploys replicas of TinyML model segments originally hosted on failed devices onto surviving devices. We formulate the joint selection of replica hosts and communication protocols as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) problem that minimizes post-reconfiguration inference latency, accounting for computation and transmission latencies, under flash memory and runtime memory constraints. Simulations using MobileNetV2 on heterogeneous IoT networks compare the proposed approach with four baselines. We implement the model in a network of 15 IoT devices with a maximum link-rate reduction of 75%, and show that MILP approach achieves an average modeled end-to-end inference latency that is 6.8% lower than that of Computation Greedy and 18.3% lower than that of Random. Index Terms TinyML, split inference, Internet of Things, fault tolerance, replica placement.

papers.title: On the Haagerup Vertex Operator Algebras
papers.abstract: Three constructions of vertex operator algebras realizing the Haagerup center were announced independently and almost simultaneously. The relations between these constructions are studied in this paper. The generators are expressed in a common lattice basis for $E_6\oplus A_2$. It is proved that the constructions of Riesen and Huang give isomorphic vertex operator algebras, and that this algebra and the algebra constructed by Jiao have isomorphic fixed point subalgebras under automorphisms of order two. The isomorphisms are given explicitly on generators. The common fixed point subalgebra contains the parafermion vertex operator algebras $K(\mathfrak{sl}_2,3)$ and $K(\mathfrak{sl}_2,13)$. A general rationality criterion for unitary vertex operator algebras is given in terms of positive linear combinations of conformal vectors and is applied to these constructions. The two vertex operator algebras are simple current extensions of the common fixed point subalgebra and have equivalent module categories as ribbon categories. The equivalence follows from decomposition with respect to a nondegenerate pointed subcategory with four simple objects in the module category of the common fixed point subalgebra. It is also proved that the conformal nets associated with these unitary vertex operator algebras are completely rational.

papers.title: Bulk and edge states in Fibonacci-Bose-Hubbard clusters
papers.abstract: We study the one- and two-boson energy subspaces of finite open Bose--Hubbard chains with Fibonacci-modulated hopping and zero on-site potential. Their spectra exhibit a hierarchy of bands and gaps, and a critical zero-energy mode for odd lengths, in agreement with prior research. For the singe-excitation subspace we find two families of length-invariant finite-energy states localized at the left cluster boundary. For the two-boson subspace, we report both doublon and separated-pair excitations in the form of Tamm/Shockley states localized near either end. In particular, the right-edge doublon states occur across all Fibonacci generations whereas the left-side states appear every second generation. We check numerically that the second-order perturbation theory accounts well for the structure of the spectrum and the edge states in the doublon subspace in the strong-coupling regime. The results are useful for future explorations of many-body physics beyond numerical tractability, specifically using near-term Josephson quantum simulators.

papers.title: Differentially Oblivious Priority Queues with Sublogarithmic Cost
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study exact online integer priority queues under differential obliviousness in the balls-and-bins model. Given a public upper bound $T$ on the number of operations and assuming that the priorities are bounded by a polynomial in $T$, we construct an $(\eps,δ)$-differentially oblivious priority queue supporting insertion and minimum extraction, which requires $\polylog(T)$ private memory. For constant $\varepsilon>0$ and $δ=\exp(-Θ(\log^2 T))$, our construction incurs $O(\log T/\log\log T)$ expected amortized total work per operation, which breaks the $Ω(\log T)$ barrier for fully oblivious priority queues~[Jacob et al., SODA'2019]. Further, we prove a matching lower bound for $(\eps,δ)$-differentially oblivious priority queues with $\varepsilon=O(1)$ and $δ=o(1)$, which indicates that our construction is asymptotically optimal in terms of total work.

papers.title: Learning to Rank Explanations for Recommendation with Language Models
papers.abstract: Recommender systems are ubiquitous on the Web, making understandable explanations essential for users. Although large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate natural-language justifications, evaluating their factual grounding and personalized relevance remains challenging. Statement-level ranking offers an alternative by selecting concise, review-derived explanations, enabling fine-grained and reproducible evaluation using established ranking metrics. However, existing statement ranking methods largely rely on collaborative representations, while semantic enhancements often fail to outperform simple user-history popularity baselines. Moreover, directly adapting language models for personalized statement ranking remains largely unexplored. In this work, we introduce LMStaR (Language Models for Statement Ranking), a fully text-based framework that formulates personalized explanation ranking as dense retrieval. A query encoder represents the user's interaction history and target-item metadata, while a statement encoder maps candidate explanations into a shared embedding space. Both encoders are jointly adapted through multi-positive contrastive learning to learn personalized relevance. Experiments on Amazon Beauty, Amazon Toys, and Yelp show that LMStaR achieves the highest NDCG@1 across all three domains, outperforming CLER by 1.06--8.25 points (+11.8--65.9%). It also leads top-five ranking on both Amazon datasets, although CLER remains stronger on Yelp. Task-specific adaptation improves all five evaluated backbones and transfers across domains without target-domain fine-tuning. Counterfactual analyses further reveal the importance of user-specific histories. These findings highlight the potential of task-adapted language models for personalized explanation ranking.

papers.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Submodular Trajectory Rewards
papers.abstract: We study cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning with decoupled dynamics and a monotone submodular reward function over joint trajectories. Due to the non-additive reward, an optimal policy may depend on the history of all agents. This dependence makes exact optimization exponential in the horizon and the number of agents. To overcome this challenge while retaining theoretical guarantees, we introduce pre-window curvature $c_m$, which quantifies how states visited more than $m$ steps earlier reduce current marginal gains. Using this curvature to control the error from restricting the policy of each agent to depend only on its last $m+1$ states, we propose a greedy algorithm that exploits the decoupled dynamics to optimize local policies sequentially. For fixed $m$, the algorithm achieves a $\frac{1-c_m}{2-c_m}$ approximation guarantee up to estimation error, and its computation time is polynomial in the number of agents and the horizon. We recover the known $1/2$-factor approximation for time-additive rewards and obtain an approximation factor no smaller than the known total-curvature bound for a single agent. We formulate multi-agent traffic monitoring as an example of this framework and evaluate our algorithm on it.

papers.title: Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field
papers.abstract: We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $Λ=π_1^{alg}(G)$, the Galois group $Θ=Gal(L/K)$ acting on $Λ$, where $L$ is a finite Galois extension of $K$ having no real places, the decomposition subgroups $Θ_v\subseteq Θ$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $Θ_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. We also compute $Sha^S(K,G)$ in some cases where $S$ contains archimedean places.

papers.title: TactiNavi: Serving and Revising an LLM Game Coach with Explicit Strategy Conditions
papers.abstract: A deployed LLM coaching agent answers requests whose correct response depends on player state and game version, so advice that is right for one player can be wrong for the next. We describe TactiNavi, the serving system behind the LLM coach of a commercial open-world game, which makes strategy applicability an explicit artifact shared by offline compilation, online execution, failure diagnosis, and release. An offline compiler turns versioned game evidence and expert guidance into strategy packages with explicit prerequisites, the serving plane evaluates those prerequisites as three-valued conditions over structured player state and records decision traces, and a control plane uses the resulting condition-rule dependencies to validate revisions on held-out traffic before release. In a retrospective evaluation of 1,122 logged coaching turns from three deployment periods, condition-bearing packages raise correctness from 57.9% to 82.0% over atomic facts and reduce strategy misapplication under changed player state from 18.1% to 10.4%, while trace-based claim verification reaches 86.4% precision at a median reply latency of 2.07 s. The deployment also showed that most apparent fixes are generation noise, because an unchanged-system rerun recovers 38.4% of failing turns and only one of 15 shipped revision units passes the release checks retrospectively. We distill these results into lessons on treating applicability as a first-class serving object, sizing traces for later diagnosis, and building the null model into the release path.

papers.title: Temporal stretching of single-photon pulses by intra-cavity frequency conversion
papers.abstract: Spectral bandwidth and frequency mismatch between quantum light emitters and quantum components is a common problem in the realization of hybrid quantum information networks. Here we propose a simultaneous solution to both of these problems by using a free-space cavity with an embedded nonlinear crystal that, through frequency conversion, facilitates perfect coupling into a cavity mode. The slow leakage of the cavity effectively stretches the photon pulse, resulting in a much longer photon pulse at a different wavelength. We show that the amount of stretching is strictly limited by the finesse and length of the cavity. Including realistic internal losses in the cavity, we show that it is possible to stretch a photon by at least two orders of magnitude with high efficiency. The proposed setup can thus constitute a valuable addition to the toolbox of quantum information technologies.

papers.title: Investigating nucleon resonances in the $pp\to K^+K^+ΛΛ$ reaction
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the \(pp \to K^+ K^+ ΛΛ\) reaction using an effective Lagrangian approach and the isobar model. The calculation includes the exchange of \(π\), \(η\), \(σ\), \(ρ\), \(ω\), and \(K\) mesons, as well as contributions from eight nucleon resonances: \(N(1535)\), \(N(1650)\), \(N(1710)\), \(N(1720)\), \(N(1895)\), \(N(1900)\), \(N(2060)\) and \(N(2120)\). The double-resonance excitation mechanism (\(NN \to N^* N^*\)) is found to dominate this reaction over the entire energy range considered. Among the exchanged mesons, the \(η\) exchange provides the largest contribution at lower energies, whereas the \(K\) exchange dominates at higher energies. Near the threshold, \(N(1535)\) and \(N(1650)\) play the most important roles, while at higher energies \(N(1710)\) and \(N(1720)\) become dominant. Due to isospin conservation, this reaction is predominantly coupled to nucleon resonances, providing a relatively clean channel for \(N^*\) spectroscopy. Our results indicate the unique potential of this reaction for studying nucleon resonances and provide a theoretical reference for future experimental studies at HIAF.

papers.title: RESTberus: Trace-Aware Benchmarking of Automated REST API Testing Tools Across Microservice Dependencies
papers.abstract: Existing REST API testing benchmarks focus on isolated services, overlooking failures arising from interactions with downstream dependencies. In microservice systems, response bodies and entry-point operations alone cannot reliably distinguish failures, compromising tool comparisons. We present RESTberus, a Kubernetes-based benchmarking platform for black-box REST API testing tools on deployed microservice systems. By complementing API-level evidence with distributed traces, RESTberus can distinguish failures manifesting in the target service from those manifesting in downstream dependencies. Across six tools on two microservice benchmarks, our trace-aware deduplication strategy achieves 87.1% accuracy, outperforming baselines from prior work by 10-13 percentage points. Our empirical study shows that all tools expose downstream failures, accounting for 11.7% of estimated unique failures on average, which isolated-service benchmarks cannot expose.
